en.title: A
en.summary: The letter name is A, as in the word Apfel.

sections.title: The letter A
paragraphs: You call this letter (A) /aː/. Its main sound is a vowel, which means open air with no touch. You hear it in (Apfel) /ˈapfəl/, which means apple. This letter makes two sounds in German.

sections.title: Pronouncing the letter
paragraphs: For the first sound, drop your jaw wide and keep your tongue low and flat. Let the air flow out freely with your voice. For the second sound, keep your mouth just as wide, but hold the tone longer. Put a hand on your throat to feel your voice shake.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: You say a short sound in a closed syllable or before a double consonant. A syllable is one beat of a word. You hear this in (Kamm) /kam/. You say a long sound when the syllable is open and stressed, or before the letter h. You hear this long sound in (Abend) /ˈaːbənt/, and also in (Bahn) /baːn/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say the vowel in cat. Drop your jaw lower, like the vowel in father. Do not glide into another sound like the vowel in day. Keep your tongue still until the sound ends.
